title: Yoroll
summary: Build playable stories without a game engine
body: Yoroll lets anyone turn stories into playable, cinematic games without coding or a game engine. Start with a script, image, or video clip, then direct the scenes, add player choices, and create branching storylines with different outcomes. AI helps bring everything together into an interactive experience you can share. It's more like directing your own interactive movie than programming a game.

title: Webless Agents
summary: Agents you want to put in front of customers
body: You wouldn’t put most website chatbots in front of a customer. Webless Agents are different: you describe the outcome you want in plain English, and Webless builds the agent on your published content, so it answers only from what you’ve said. You review every instruction and change anything before it goes live. Then it gets to work: answering questions, qualifying buyers, sending quotes, booking meetings and handing off to your team. For Product Hunt: 3 months of our highest plan, free.

title: Omi CLI
summary: AI coding agents that work while you're away.
body: Omi can build anything. Give Omi a coding task and let it get to work: it reads your repo, fixes bugs, runs tests, and uses a real browser to check your app. Parallel subagents tackle tasks in separate worktrees. Background agents keep going after you close the terminal; cloud agents can open PRs. Review changes as diffs, undo mistakes, and choose from 13 models or bring your own. Free to start: npm i -g @builditomi/cli

body: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong semantic understanding but remain limited in their ability to reason about metric 3D space in the physical world. Existing VLMs typically infer 3D scene structure from one or more images without known camera calibration or cross-view geometric constraints. This makes metric 3D inference inherently ambiguous and leaves it unclear whether their spatial predictions are grounded in visual evidence or driven primarily by semantic priors. In contrast, calibrated stereo provides explicit cross-view geometry that resolves this ambiguity and offers a more reliable foundation for metric 3D perception and geometric generalization.
